text: More than 1,000 years ago, the Slavic peoples lived across central, eastern and south-eastern Europe.
They worshipped a god of the sky and thunder, Perun, and spirits of waters, forests, fields and homes.
src: The Early Slavs, from the 5th to the 10th centuries CE, lived across central, eastern and southeastern Europe
The Slavs worshipped a supreme god of the sky and thunder, later known as Perun / a host of spirits of waters, forests, fields, households and ancestors

text: In the west, temples held idols with many heads, like the four-headed Svetovid at Arkona.
Priests called volkhvs kept the temples and led the festivals.
src: West Slavic temples held many-headed idols, such as the four-headed Svetovid at Arkona
Priests called volkhvs kept the temples and led rituals and festivals

text: In Kievan Rus’, Vladimir the Great was baptised, made a Christian, together with his people.
src: Rulers adopted Christianity in Great Moravia (863), Bulgaria (864), Poland (966) and Kievan Rus’ (988)
Vladimir is baptised with his subjects

text: The old idols of Kiev were burned or thrown into the river Dnieper.
Later, Christianity was forced on the West Slavs of the Baltic, and the temple of Svetovid was destroyed.
src: the idols of Kiev are burned or thrown into the Dnieper
The West Slavs of the Baltic held out longest / Catholicism was imposed by force in the Northern Crusades / Bishop Absalon destroyed the temple of Svetovid

text: The Slavs left no holy books, so we know their faith from others, such as the writers of old chronicles.
But the old gods lived on for centuries in folk customs and festivals.
src: No original mythological texts survive, so Slavic religion is known from outsiders, from Christian writers and from reconstruction / the Rus’ chronicles
the old gods lived on for centuries in folk religion / Much lived on in folk religion: the rites of Koliada, Kupala and Marzanna
